analysis: The code snippet creates a new IOException using the single-argument String constructor, which does not set a cause. Then it calls initCause(e) where e is a different IOException caught from waitForChannelSuccessOrFailure. Since the new IOException is not created with a cause constructor and initCause has not been called before, IllegalStateException cannot occur. Since e is a different object (not the same as the new IOException), IllegalArgumentException cannot occur. Thus both exceptions are fully avoided in this context.
remark: In this code, initCause is called on a newly created IOException without a pre-set cause, and the argument e is a different Throwable instance. Therefore neither exception from initCause will be thrown.
